issues.description: Lecture constructor parameter order is inconsistent between the problem statement (UML and text) and the solution implementation. Problem statement (UML and instruction) requires the constructor parameters to follow the UML attribute order: numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors. The solution implements a constructor with signature: Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors). The template only contains a TODO for adding the constructor. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected constructor signature and parameter ordering required by tests or examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferable to match the written UML/instructions): change the solution constructor signature to match the UML order, e.g. public Lecture(int numberOfInscribedStudents, String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfTutors) and update the constructor body and any examples/tests accordingly; update the template to include the same signature or an instructive TODO showing the expected parameter order. Option B: if the intended order is to have lectureName first, update the UML block and the textual instruction that mandates following the UML order so they list lectureName first and match the solution. Ensure template, problem text, UML diagram, and solution all use the same constructor parameter ordering.
